results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 34 outline summaries match the controlling ideas of p01 to p34 in spec order; the KEY POINTS callout matches the thesis statement and no paragraph.
The reverse outline lists the same controlling ideas in the same order as the spec's sections and paragraphs.

Four flagged units hold one idea: Sixteen Ways ¶2 (the patterns chain, with its example and a closing use), Evidence ¶5 (what the two companies publish, which is why they are the anchors), Larkfield ¶2 (the incidents and the program that answers them), Draws On ¶1 (what the book rests on, with the model set apart as not a source).

results.quote: I write as an architect who builds on payment providers; where I give a judgement I say “I” and give my reasons.
results.finding: The unit holds what the book assumes and explains (prior knowledge, terms, glossary) and, unrelated to it, whose voice the book speaks in. The spec's controlling idea joins the same two with 'and it speaks as'.

results.draft_locus: Start With the Decision in Front of You ¶3
results.quote: You can also read by role, and for the decision itself the [[toolkit]] collects sixteen working cards, such as the idempotency key card and the reconciliation card.
results.finding: Routes by role and the toolkit's cards are two ideas in one sentence, and the list that follows serves only the first; both flow readers called them unrelated (A item 18, B item 21). The spec's controlling idea is double in the same way.

results.quote: I developed the book through AI-mediated authoring: I set the concept, structure and arguments; AI tools supported research, drafting, cross-checks and editing; I reviewed and decided.
results.finding: The unit holds the book's currency (living journal, cut-off of 17 November 2026, scenes in 2027, check the source) and how it was made and who answers for it (spec link, AI-mediated authoring, responsibility). The spec's controlling idea lists both; flow reader B (item 25) found the paragraph is not about what its heading says.
Every unit ties to a supporting claim: audience, organization and routes to S2; argument and patterns to S1; evidence to S3 and S4; Larkfield, left-out and basis to S5.

The promises table and Figure 1 are followed by 'It follows that the API's answer is not the outcome'; the layout table by the prerequisite order and Figure 2 by its caption; the 2017 posts, the two corrected absences and the volume figures each get a sentence on what they show; the sample rows are explained by the sentence that introduces them; the routing table by the paragraph on its surprising row.

results.draft_locus: The Argument: A Promise That Takes Days to Keep ¶4
results.quote: on 1 July 2026 Adyen closed two acquisitions
results.finding: The spec gives this fact to show Adyen adding bought products in 2026, but the draft does not say what was acquired or what the fact shows; the closing 'a sequence, not two territories' does not connect it. Both flow readers could not tell what it is evidence of (A item 5, B item 6).

All other declared transitions are expressed at their boundaries (for example 'It follows that', 'The opposite view is', 'When a system records one of those promises as the truth', 'Where no source speaks', 'The same separation applies', 'One row starts somewhere you might not expect'). The openings of the organization, evidence, routes and left-out sections lean on their headings and carry the declared known information only loosely, but neither flow reader lost the link there.

results.quote: Stripe and Adyen are the anchors because both publish enough to compare, not because either is the right answer for every business.
results.finding: Declared as additional support carrying over 'dated facts and dated absences about two companies'; the sentence picks up neither and starts a new subject after the paragraph on corrected absences. Flow reader B (item 13): 'The move from search errors to the choice of companies has no transition'; reader A (item 13) found it out of place.

results.finding: The opening is a dated scene, a contrast that leads to a disputable claim, and a roadmap; none of the weak patterns.
The conclusion synthesizes, returns to the opening scene and hands off; it opens with no formula, holds no body evidence and adds no new subtopic.

It says what no section says alone (one discipline applied to a payment, a sentence about a provider and an example; the book asks of itself what it asks the reader to build) and turns it into what the reader does: 'do not record a promise as the truth'. The so-what is given as that instruction, less explicitly than the spec's wording about not treating a post or this book as a description of today's system.
'You can now read Mila's screen' returns to the opening payment and gives the bank's promise, the Thursday payout and the open period until about 7 July.
The cold reader predicted every roadmap item in order and the kind of evidence (one fictional payment, a few dated facts about what the two companies publish).
The prediction from the opening alone contains each element of the expected answer in the expected order, with the expected evidence.
The answer states the argument (the instant answer is the first of several promises; components close the gap without losing or duplicating money) and lists the ten parts' subjects in order.

The answer names idempotency-and-retries (Part IV) first, then webhooks and state machines, and gives the page's reason: the reliability chapter is about keeping the path up, not about an unknown outcome.

All four statements are labeled as expected (documented fact with source and year, author's inference, fictional illustration, assumption that is not a benchmark), each with how far to rely on it; for (a) the answer gives the own-definition caveat through the unranked volume figures.

The answer says revenue cannot be compared (Adyen audited net revenue, Stripe volume and no revenue, volumes not ranked) and that the idempotency post is from 2017, nine years old, checked against current documentation for the interface only. Two details of the expected answer are absent from the draft and so from the answer, neither changing the ruling: Stripe's customer counts and Adyen's 2021 account of a key database.
